2000-03-20: Angela Merkel was endorsed by the Christian Democrat Union executive as its preferred nominee for party leader, assuring her of winning the party chairmanship at a conference next month.
2005-05-22: Angela Merkel emerged as the conservative opposition's undisputed challenger to Chancellor Gerhard Schröder after he announced he would seek an early general election.
2005-06-24: A new biography raises embarrassing questions about Angela Merkel's early life in communist East Germany and suggests her father actively collaborated with the communist regime.
2005-07-25: Opinion polls show Angela Merkel's hopes of becoming Germany's first woman chancellor are threatened by the new Left party, which is polling in third place.
2005-08-16: Angela Merkel presented her campaign team for the upcoming general election, introducing nine members likely to play leading roles in a Merkel-led cabinet.
2005-09-05: Aides to Angela Merkel admitted that her closing speech in a televised election debate was closely modelled on Ronald Reagan's 1980 debate remarks.
2005-09-06: Doris Schröder-Kopf, wife of Chancellor Gerhard Schröder, rebuked Angela Merkel, saying Merkel had done nothing to help German women and had been a disaster as minister for women.
2005-09-11: Angela Merkel’s Christian Democratic party has seen its lead slip ahead of Germany’s general election, and it remains unclear whether she will become chancellor.
2005-09-17: Angela Merkel's Christian Democrats and Gerhard Schröder's Social Democrats both claim a mandate to form a government after neither wins a majority in Germany's general election, leaving Merkel likely able to become chancellor only through a grand coalition.
2005-09-18: The Greens appeared to rule out joining a coalition with Angela Merkel's conservative CDU party, dealing a setback to her chances of becoming Germany's next chancellor.
Angela Merkel's CDU/CSU party narrowly edged out Gerhard Schröder's SPD by four seats and one percentage point in the German election.
2005-09-20: Angela Merkel wins a vote of confidence from her parliamentary party, with 98% of Christian Democratic MPs reconfirming her as their leader, ahead of coalition talks beginning tomorrow.
2005-09-21: Angela Merkel is scheduled to hold talks with Chancellor Gerhard Schröder about a possible grand coalition following an inconclusive election, while insisting she be chancellor.
2005-10-02: Angela Merkel's Christian Democrat party narrowly won a delayed general election vote in Dresden, increasing her narrow lead over the Social Democrats from three to four seats.
2005-10-04: Angela Merkel held talks with Chancellor Gerhard Schröder and said she was more optimistic that a "grand coalition" could work, amid speculation Schröder might resign and pave the way for her to become Germany's first woman chancellor.
2005-10-09: Angela Merkel agrees a deal to become Germany's first woman chancellor, leading a grand coalition after Gerhard Schröder resigns.
2005-10-10: Angela Merkel is set to become Germany's first female chancellor after rival Gerhard Schröder agreed to a grand coalition between her Christian Democrats and his Social Democrats.
2005-10-11: Angela Merkel, leader of the Christian Democrat party, gained the chancellorship of Germany, though with a narrow victory that forced her to give eight of fourteen ministries to the Social Democrats.
2005-11-01: Senior conservative Edmund Stoiber announced he would not serve in a grand coalition under Angela Merkel, deepening Germany's political crisis and casting doubt on whether Merkel would become chancellor.
2005-11-11: Germany's two biggest parties agreed a formal coalition deal, allowing Angela Merkel to take over as chancellor on November 22.
2005-11-12: Chancellor-designate Angela Merkel promised to restore Germany’s standing in Europe and announced austerity measures, including a VAT increase, after her Christian Democrats reached a coalition deal with the Social Democrats.
2005-11-14: Angela Merkel's Christian Democrat party and the Social Democrats approved a historic coalition agreement that will make her Germany's first female chancellor.
2005-11-22: Angela Merkel was sworn in as Germany's first female chancellor and first leader from the former East Germany, leading a grand coalition after winning a Bundestag vote of 397 to 202.
2006-03-25: A security camera on the roof of Berlin's Pergamon Museum had been filming Chancellor Angela Merkel's private flat for eight years, prompting a federal police investigation.
2006-06-02: German Chancellor Angela Merkel held talks in Berlin with UK Chancellor Gordon Brown on European economic reform and backed his new global business forum.
2006-06-08: German Chancellor Angela Merkel made her first regular video podcast broadcast, with a mobile phone version being planned.
2006-10-08: Angela Merkel faces plummeting poll ratings and a revolt within her conservative Christian Democrat party nearly a year after becoming Germany's first female chancellor.
2006-11-03: Tony Blair urges German Chancellor Angela Merkel to push for an international climate change agreement when Germany assumes the G8 presidency.
2007-03-07: German Chancellor Angela Merkel chairs the EU spring summit and urges EU leaders to commit to a unilateral 20% cut in greenhouse gas emissions by 2020.
2007-03-08: German Chancellor Angela Merkel, chairing the EU spring summit, urged EU leaders to commit to a unilateral 20% cut in greenhouse gas emissions by 2020, but faced opposition from France and other countries over nuclear power and binding renewable energy targets.
2007-03-24: German Chancellor Angela Merkel told the prime ministers or presidents of 27 countries at the EU's 50th birthday summit in Berlin that modern Europe was a dream come true, and used the summit to push for reviving the European constitution.
2007-05-01: Angela Merkel, as current EU president and German Chancellor, prepares to host the G8 summit in Heiligendamm in June, with her leadership style and domestic economic improvements noted.
2007-07-16: Gordon Brown is to make his first foreign visit as British prime minister to Berlin to have supper with Angela Merkel.
2007-09-23: German Chancellor Angela Merkel met with the Dalai Lama despite China's warnings, prompting China to cancel a planned meeting between a German minister and Chinese officials.
2007-11-13: German Vice-Chancellor Franz Müntefering, a leading figure in Angela Merkel's coalition government, resigned, dealing a blow to Merkel's efforts to keep the grand coalition intact.
2008-01-07: German Chancellor Angela Merkel backed a controversial plan to introduce boot camps and "warning shot" spells in prison for criminal youths, saying the measures were necessary to give Germany an "atmosphere of basic security."
2008-03-14: German Chancellor Angela Merkel secured concessions at an EU summit to protect several of Germany's heavy industries from the EU's climate change plan, potentially jeopardizing Europe's post-Kyoto climate accord.
2008-06-15: Angela Merkel and Nicolas Sarkozy agreed on a 2020 emissions target of between 95 and 110 grams of CO2 per kilometre for new cars, resolving a dispute over previous emissions goals.
2008-09-17: Angela Merkel said in an interview with Frau im Spiegel that she wished she could do gymnastics on the balance beam, while acknowledging it is not her forte.
2008-09-24: The European Parliament's environment committee rejected a Franco-German compromise backed by Angela Merkel and Nicolas Sarkozy that would have weakened EU proposals to cut carbon dioxide emissions from new cars.
2009-01-27: Angela Merkel's Christian Democrats introduce an "old banger bonus" as part of a €50bn stimulus package, offering €2,500 to owners of cars nine years or older who trade them in for new or nearly new models.
2009-03-31: German Chancellor Angela Merkel addressed 3,000 Opel workers at the Rüsselsheim car plant but failed to set out a clear plan to save the car company from being brought down by the likely insolvency of its US parent, General Motors.
2009-08-23: German Chancellor Angela Merkel demands a quick resolution to protracted negotiations over the takeover of Opel, General Motors' European business, expressing regret at GM's failure to choose Magna and saying a decision is urgently needed.
2009-08-24: German Chancellor Angela Merkel said a resolution to the question of General Motors' Opel/Vauxhall future was "urgently needed."
2009-09-12: Angela Merkel participated in the sole televised election debate against Foreign Minister Frank-Walter Steinmeier, with a viewer poll giving Steinmeier a 31-21 margin of victory while 48% considered it a draw.
2009-09-13: Angela Merkel debated Social Democrat challenger Frank-Walter Steinmeier in a 90-minute live television debate ahead of the German federal election.
2009-09-21: Chancellor Angela Merkel seeks a clear signal from the Free Democrats (FDP) that they would be ready to form a centre-right government with her Christian Democratic Union (CDU) ahead of the general election.
2009-09-25: Angela Merkel is expected to win the German general election, but coalition options remain unclear.
2009-09-27: Angela Merkel is seeking re-election as chancellor in Germany's general election, with polls open and her expected to remain chancellor.
2010-05-08: German Chancellor Angela Merkel faces a crucial state election in North Rhine-Westphalia, with polls indicating her Christian Democrats and Free Democrats are likely to be defeated.
2010-05-09: Angela Merkel's Christian Democrats suffer a bruising defeat in the North Rhine Westphalia regional election, with voters punishing her perceived dithering over the Greek bailout, costing her coalition its majority in the Bundesrat.
2010-05-22: German Chancellor Angela Merkel announced a ban on naked shorting, a move markets interpreted as erratic regulatory spite, resulting in more panic selling.
2010-06-05: German Chancellor Angela Merkel faces deepening political troubles after the resignation of President Horst Köhler and other party setbacks, with coalition leaders meeting to discuss budget cuts.
2010-07-15: Peter Mandelson advised Angela Merkel to engage with David Cameron rather than sever ties after he abandoned the main centre-right grouping in the European Parliament.
2010-08-30: German Chancellor Angela Merkel announced an extension of the nation's nuclear power plant operations for up to 15 years beyond the scheduled phase-out.
German Chancellor Angela Merkel called on Germany's central bank to dismiss board member Thilo Sarrazin over his remarks about Jews and Muslim immigrants.
2010-09-06: German Chancellor Angela Merkel hailed the government's agreement to extend the working lives of the country's nuclear reactors by an average of 12 years as a "revolution in energy provision."
2011-02-20: Angela Merkel's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) suffered a humiliating defeat in the Hamburg regional election, losing control of the city-state to the opposition SPD, which won an absolute majority.
2011-03-02: Angela Merkel appoints her closest adviser Thomas de Maizière as Germany's defence minister, succeeding Karl-Theodor zu Guttenberg, who resigned over a plagiarism scandal.
2011-03-12: Angela Merkel ordered immediate safety checks on all of Germany's nuclear power stations following the crisis in Fukushima, Japan.
2011-03-13: Angela Merkel is expected to announce the suspension of plans to extend the life of Germany's nuclear power stations following Japan's nuclear emergency.
2011-03-14: Following the Fukushima disaster, German Chancellor Angela Merkel faces calls to alter her pro-nuclear stance and reverse the decision to extend the operating lives of Germany's nuclear power plants.
2011-03-15: Angela Merkel announces the temporary closure of seven of Germany's nuclear power stations built before 1980 pending a safety review.
2011-03-27: Voters in Baden-Württemberg ousted Angela Merkel's centre-right CDU for the first time in half a century, handing power to what is likely to become Germany's first Green party-led state coalition.
2011-05-22: Angela Merkel's Christian Democratic Union party suffered a symbolic election blow in Bremen as the Green party won more votes than the CDU for the first time in a state election.
Angela Merkel said 2022 was "the right space of time" as a goal for Germany's total withdrawal from nuclear power, without herself committing to a firm date for decommissioning.
2011-05-30: Angela Merkel committed to shutting down all of Germany's nuclear reactors by 2022, prompted by Japan's nuclear disaster.
2011-09-29: Angela Merkel won a Bundestag vote 523 to 85 to increase the euro bailout mechanism's powers, approving an increase of Germany's guarantees from €123bn to €211bn.
2011-10-26: Angela Merkel put her plans for the latest euro rescue package to a vote in the Bundestag, winning 503 out of 596 votes, which she could use as a mandate at the Brussels summits.
2011-12-05: Angela Merkel and Nicolas Sarkozy are to discuss a new "fiscal union" to underpin the euro at their Paris meeting.
2012-02-17: German President Christian Wulff, handpicked by Angela Merkel, resigned amid a corruption scandal, forcing Merkel to cancel a trip to Rome and raising questions about her judgment.
2012-04-27: Angela Merkel said she was not prepared to bow to François Hollande's desire to renegotiate the framework for EU budgetary discipline, defending the fiscal pact as not open to alteration.
2012-05-06: Voters in the Schleswig-Holstein state election appeared to reject the governing centre-right CDU-FDP coalition, ending the CDU-FDP leadership in the state and increasing pressure on Angela Merkel to end her collaboration with the FDP.
If Francois Hollande wins the French presidency, he plans to make Berlin his first stop to tell Angela Merkel that her fiscal pact must be re-opened.
2012-05-13: Angela Merkel's Christian Democrats suffered a heavy defeat in North Rhine-Westphalia's state election, losing to the centre-left SPD in what was seen as a backlash against her European austerity campaign.
2012-06-29: Angela Merkel made concessions at an EU summit, including agreeing to direct eurozone bank recapitalization and granting private creditors equal status with the bailout fund in the Spanish rescue.
2012-08-17: German Chancellor Angela Merkel refused to make a quick decision on granting Greece more time to meet its bailout targets, saying solutions would not be found that Friday.
2012-10-30: Hitachi buys the Horizon nuclear power business, which had been abandoned by RWE and E.on after the Fukushima disaster led Angela Merkel to turn her back on building new reactors.
2012-12-04: Angela Merkel was re-elected as leader of the Christian Democrats (CDU) for the seventh time, with a record vote approaching 98%.
2013-01-20: Angela Merkel's ruling centre-right coalition suffered a setback in the Lower Saxony regional election as the centre-left opposition secured a wafer-thin one-seat majority.
2013-01-21: Angela Merkel's centre-right coalition was narrowly ousted by the opposition centre-left in the Lower Saxony regional election, a result she called "emotionally difficult" and which dealt a blow to her hopes for re-election in September.
2013-01-23: German Chancellor Angela Merkel gives a guarded response to David Cameron's EU referendum speech, indicating openness to negotiating a "fair compromise" on Britain's EU membership terms.
2013-06-29: Angela Merkel's government derailed an EU compromise deal on car emissions after receiving a letter from German car manufacturers association president Matthias Wissmann warning that Germany's premium car sector should not be destroyed by carbon limits.
2013-09-01: Angela Merkel participated in a televised debate with Peer Steinbrück during the German election campaign.
2013-09-15: Voters in Bavaria handed a resounding victory to allies of Angela Merkel, with the Christian Social Union winning an absolute majority a week before the national election.
2013-09-22: Angela Merkel's Christian Democratic Union and its sister party won 41.5% of the vote in Germany's federal election, securing a historic third term for Merkel.
2013-09-23: Angela Merkel confirms she has had initial informal talks with the SPD about a possible grand coalition, while ruling out minority rule.
Angela Merkel celebrates victory in German election.
2013-10-15: Germany's Green party announced it would no longer continue coalition talks with Angela Merkel's CDU, most likely opting for political opposition instead.
2013-11-27: Angela Merkel's CDU party reached an agreement to form a coalition government with the Social Democrats, pending an SPD member ballot.
2013-12-15: Ursula von der Leyen is appointed as Germany's first female defence minister, triggering speculation about whether she is being groomed to succeed Angela Merkel as leader of the Christian Democrats.
2014-01-29: Angela Merkel used the first speech of her third term to criticize US surveillance activities, saying a programme where the end justifies all means violates trust, while also calling the US Germany's best ally.
2014-03-10: German Chancellor Angela Merkel asked David Cameron at the CeBIT exhibition in Germany when the UK would complete its rollout of broadband to rural areas.
2014-05-02: German Chancellor Angela Merkel made her first visit to the White House since revelations that the NSA had bugged her calls, holding a frosty joint appearance with President Barack Obama that was dominated by Ukraine and included only a brief, inconclusive exchange on NSA surveillance.
2014-05-25: Angela Merkel's CDU/CSU won Germany's European parliamentary election with 35.4% of the vote, despite it being the party's worst result in the history of European elections.
2014-07-17: Angela Merkel turned 60 and thanked a German reporter who sang the traditional birthday song at a news conference in Brussels, revealing that other leaders had given her flowers.
2014-10-17: Angela Merkel has remained Germany's chancellor as the one constant throughout the eurozone crisis, during which 54 different leaders have headed eurozone member countries since she took office in 2005.
2015-01-25: Syriza's election victory in Greece delivers an unambiguous defeat for Angela Merkel and her austerity-based strategy for sustaining the euro.
2015-03-23: Greek Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras warned Angela Merkel that Greece cannot meet looming debt repayments without urgent aid, ahead of their first face-to-face talks in Berlin.
2015-07-15: Angela Merkel comforts a sobbing Palestinian teenage refugee after telling her that Germany cannot help all refugees, during a televised meeting with students in Rostock.
2015-07-17: Angela Merkel faces a Bundestag vote on a third Greek bailout, with about 50 MPs from her ruling alliance expected to rebel and vote no.
2015-08-04: The verb "merkeln," meaning to be indecisive, is on track to become Germany's most popular "youth word" of the year in a Langenscheidt poll, reflecting Angela Merkel's influence on German slang.
2015-08-31: German Chancellor Angela Merkel urged other EU countries to take in more refugees and renewed her call for a quota system to share asylum seekers among the 28-nation bloc.
2015-09-08: German Chancellor Angela Merkel warned that even if EU Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker secures agreement on a plan to relocate 160,000 asylum seekers, the proposals might not be enough to make a dent in the refugee crisis.
2015-09-14: Angela Merkel's decision to close Germany's borders left refugees stranded in Vienna, reversing an earlier open-border policy.
2015-09-15: Angela Merkel defended her decision to open German borders to unregistered refugees and rejected claims it worsened Europe's refugee crisis, speaking after Germany introduced border controls.
2015-10-15: Angela Merkel rejected criticism of her open-door refugee policy in a Bundestag speech, calling the crisis a historic test for Europe and pressing for EU solidarity ahead of a Brussels summit.
2015-10-28: Angela Merkel flies to China on a trade visit accompanied by Volkswagen chief Matthias Müller to promote German trading interests and limit damage from the diesel emissions scandal.
2015-10-30: Angela Merkel faces mounting pressure to stem the flow of refugees into Germany ahead of an emergency summit with government leaders, amid coalition tensions and criticism from CSU leader Horst Seehofer.
2015-11-05: Angela Merkel suffered a setback as her plan to set up "transit zones" on the border with Austria was rejected at crisis talks in Berlin, with the government instead announcing up to five "reception centres" inside Germany.
2015-12-09: Time magazine named German chancellor Angela Merkel its Person of the Year, citing her leadership during the Greek debt crisis and her encouragement of countries to open borders to migrants and refugees.
2016-02-10: Bavarian leader Horst Seehofer accused Angela Merkel of pursuing a "rule of injustice" in her handling of the refugee crisis, escalating a rebellion by the CSU against the German chancellor.
2016-02-17: German Chancellor Angela Merkel defended her open-door refugee policy ahead of an EU summit, while a growing majority of EU states opposed her approach and Austria announced stricter border controls.
2016-03-09: Angela Merkel faces a key test of her refugee policies in German regional elections, with her CDU party at risk of losing its status as the biggest party in Baden-Württemberg.
2016-03-12: Angela Merkel faces pressure from the far right and the refugee crisis ahead of elections in three German states, with her Christian Democratic Union expected to be punished by voters over her open-door refugee policy.
2016-04-14: German Chancellor Angela Merkel announces Germany's first-ever integration law requiring asylum seekers to integrate into society in return for being allowed to live and work in the country.
2016-04-23: German Chancellor Angela Merkel visited southern Turkey to inaugurate the EU's new aid programme for Syrian refugees, amid accusations that she is turning a blind eye to their plight and validating Turkey's authoritarianism.
2016-06-06: German President Joachim Gauck announced he will not stand for a second term, creating difficulties for Chancellor Angela Merkel and triggering a cross-party race for his successor ahead of the 2017 general election.
2016-07-20: German Chancellor Angela Merkel greeted UK Prime Minister Theresa May in Berlin for bilateral talks, with Brexit expected to be the major subject.
2016-07-25: Pressure grows on Angela Merkel to start closing Germany's open door after four deadly incidents of violence in a single week.
2016-07-28: Angela Merkel defended her open-door refugee policy and rejected guilt over recent violent attacks in Germany, announcing a nine-point security plan.
2016-09-04: Angela Merkel's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) came third in the Mecklenburg-Vorpommern regional election, behind the Social Democrats and the rightwing populist Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), a result widely seen as a rebuke over her refugee crisis management.
2016-09-18: Angela Merkel's CDU party suffers its lowest-ever result in the Berlin state election, placing second with 17.5% behind the Social Democrats, in the party's fourth consecutive electoral setback.
2016-09-19: Angela Merkel admitted mistakes in her handling of the 2015 refugee crisis and took responsibility for her party's disastrous showing in the Berlin state election.
2016-11-20: Angela Merkel announces she will run for a fourth term as German chancellor in 2017.
2016-11-23: Angela Merkel announced that she planned to stand for a fourth term as Chancellor.
2016-11-24: Martin Schulz announced he is leaving EU politics to seek a seat in the German Bundestag, fuelling speculation that he could enter the race to challenge Angela Merkel in the 2017 federal elections.
2017-01-24: Martin Schulz announced as the SPD's candidate to challenge Angela Merkel in the 2017 German elections and as the new SPD leader, with Sigmar Gabriel resigning that post to become German foreign minister.
2017-01-28: German Chancellor Angela Merkel, in a phone call with President Donald Trump, explained the obligations of the refugee convention and expressed regret over his executive order banning travel from seven Muslim-majority countries.
2017-02-15: Polls show the SPD under Martin Schulz rising to a five-year high, three points behind Angela Merkel’s Christian Democrats, and a theoretical direct chancellor vote puts Schulz at 37% to Merkel’s 38%.
2017-03-17: Angela Merkel is scheduled to meet Donald Trump at the White House for the first time, with her agenda focused on trade and selling German cars rather than lecturing on liberal values.
2017-06-16: Angela Merkel said her former mentor Helmut Kohl was “the right man at the right time,” who seized a “historic chance” to overcome the divide running through Europe.
2017-07-10: Allies of German Chancellor Angela Merkel call for new curbs on leftwing extremists, including a Europe-wide register, after her decision to hold the G20 summit in Hamburg ended in violent clashes and injuries to nearly 500 police officers.
2017-09-05: Angela Merkel, addressing the Bundestag for the final time in the parliamentary term, promised to do everything in her powers to prevent court-enforced diesel bans in German cities.
2017-09-24: Angela Merkel's Christian Democrats win the German federal election but with their worst result since 1949, leaving Merkel isolated as she seeks a coalition government.
